Usage: memoriahub android [options] [command]

Build, sign, version and publish the Android app

Options:
  --repo <path>            MemoriaHub checkout to use (else
                           MEMORIAHUB_REPO_ROOT, else the nearest ancestor with
                           apps/android)
  -h, --help               display help for command

Commands:
  doctor [options]         Check the JDK, Android SDK, Gradle wrapper, keystore
                           and login; --fix installs what it can
  keystore                 Manage the release signing keystore
                           (~/.memoriahub/android)
  version [options]        Show or change apps/android/version.properties (every
                           change also increments versionCode)
  build [options]          Build and sign the APK into dist/android/ with a
                           sidecar metadata JSON
  publish [options] [apk]  Upload a built APK (default: the newest in
                           dist/android) to the logged-in server
  releases [options]       List the server's releases (current marked *);
                           `releases current <id>` makes one current (rollback)
  release [options]        Pre-check, then bump → build → publish as current →
                           commit version.properties
  help [command]           display help for command

Environment:
  MEMORIAHUB_REPO_ROOT     checkout to use when --repo is not given
  MEMORIAHUB_GRADLE_ARGS   extra arguments appended to every Gradle run (e.g. "--no-daemon --max-workers=1")
  GRADLE_OPTS, JAVA_HOME   passed to Gradle unchanged
  ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD / ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD   keystore passwords for `keystore init|import`

First release on a fresh machine:
  memoriahub login
  memoriahub android doctor --fix --yes
  memoriahub android keystore init        # then BACK UP ~/.memoriahub/android/
  memoriahub android release --bump patch --notes "…"
